outcome: pain levels (measured by McGill Pain Questionnaire)
stress levels (measured by Psychological Stress Measure)
cohort: 120 women, 60 who underwent cesarean section and 60 who had a vaginal delivery
finding: Women who underwent cesarean section experienced higher pain levels, particularly in the lower abdomen, back, breast, and shoulders, while women who had a vaginal delivery reported higher stress levels at discharge.
mod_finding: Women who underwent cesarean delivery experienced higher levels of pain compared to those who delivered vaginally.
